staticFindings: Each readiness fixture has a unique mkdtempSync hsk-readiness-* directory and Git commands run synchronously with its own cwd/index.
No test suite process.chdir or process.env mutation was found during the targeted parallel/environment inspection; separate package fixtures also use unique temporary directories.
Git parent config and inherited environment remain in force. Diagnostics record GIT_* variable names only, never their values; no global config or environment mutation was added.
A permanent inherited initialization failure does not explain the observed second-add-only failure without additional evidence; the initial fixture init/add/commit succeeded.
The old constructor lacked cleanup on setup failure because withFixture() only enters try/finally after fixture() returns. A controlled injected init failure proves this distinct cleanup defect.

implementation.scope: Only readiness test fixture helper and a dedicated diagnostic runner; no application runtime, release gate assertions, workflow, production assets or source content modified by this agent.
implementation.stderr: Capture stdout and stderr, command argv/cwd/exit status/signal/error code, cwd/index/index.lock file state, and inherited GIT_* variable names.
implementation.failureSemantics: Re-throw a diagnostic error with the original cause. No retries, swallowed failures, automatic lock removal, or claimed root-cause repair.
implementation.constructorCleanup: Remove the uniquely created temporary directory after any constructor failure; retain the original error and attach cleanup error metadata if cleanup itself fails.

outputIsolation.resolution: Absolute or relative env path resolved with path.resolve; fallback to script directory only when no override is supplied. All generated JSON and TAP files use the selected output directory.

controlledProbes: Actual helper with explicitly held synthetic .git/index.lock returns 128 and records command/cwd/status/stderr/lock state; repeated call remains rejected.
Actual add succeeds after the probe explicitly removes its own synthetic lock.
Original baseline fixture leaves its unique directory behind after an injected constructor init failure; the diagnostic runner detects and then cleans it.
Current actual fixture cleans its unique directory on the same injected constructor failure and preserves diagnostics.
authorVerification.syntheticIsNotHistorical: These probes deliberately induce failures to test observability/cleanup; they are not a reproduction or diagnosis of the historical CI failure.
authorVerification.runtime: Local locked dependencies, Node v24.19.0, git version 2.51.1, linux
authorVerification.broaderCI: Not executed by this agent in this report; parent owns the new native CI matrix and its independent review.

integration.excludeGeneratedLocalOutputs: Do not treat local helper-negative-probes.json, stress-results.json or stress-run-*.tap as source-code inputs for safe source commit; collect fresh CI outputs under .repro-output. Local report pins are observation records only.
integration.expectedSuccess: 12 processes, each 9 actual tests with no skipped/cancelled/todo cases, four controlled probes, source bytes stable. Any nonzero child or failing metric makes the runner fail.
integration.approval: Independent review required by the parent; this author report does not self-certify independent acceptance.

remainingRisk: The original CI exit 128 root cause cannot be recovered from discarded stderr. If it recurs, the new diagnostic failure should preserve useful command/path/status/error context; no prevention claim is made.
